story.title: Senate Judiciary Committee Postpones Vote on Todd Blanche's Attorney General Nomination
story.summary: The Senate Judiciary Committee has postponed a key vote on Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general, amid concerns from two Republican senators. The delay raises questions about Blanche's confirmation as President Trump's pick for the position, particularly in light of issues related to Trump's IRS lawsuit. The Department of Justice has expressed its willingness to work with the senators to advance the nomination.

explore_lenses.label: What did the postponement change?
explore_lenses.title: The nomination remains in committee
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate change is procedural: the Judiciary Committee did not take its planned vote to send Todd Blanche’s nomination to the full Senate. The delay leaves negotiations over the IRS settlement unresolved rather than deciding Blanche’s nomination on the merits.

claims.text: A committee spokesperson said the vote was postponed while work continued to secure enough support to report Blanche’s nomination favorably.
Blanche was nominated by President Trump on June 8 and had already appeared before the Judiciary Committee for a nomination hearing on July 15.
The postponement is not a rejection or a Senate confirmation vote; it prevents the nomination from being reported to the Senate at this time.

explore_lenses.label: Why are Cornyn and Tillis holding up the vote?
explore_lenses.title: They seek written limits on the IRS deal
explore_lenses.summary: Republican Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis are focused on the settlement of Trump’s IRS lawsuit, not a generalized objection to Blanche’s qualifications. Their stated concern is whether the agreement could protect Trump and relatives beyond already-existing tax audits.

claims.text: Cornyn and Tillis sought written confirmation that the proposed $1.776 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund is definitively abandoned and clarification of the settlement’s tax-audit protections.
Cornyn said he wants the settlement changed to state clearly that it covers existing audits only, rather than future tax filings.
At his hearing, Blanche characterized the settlement as an agreement ending past audits, while acknowledging that it discharged liability connected to past filings.
DOJ said after the postponement that it remained ready to work productively with Cornyn and Tillis to advance the confirmation.

explore_lenses.label: What must happen before a final Senate vote?
explore_lenses.title: Committee action must resume first
explore_lenses.summary: For a normal confirmation path, the Judiciary Committee must take further action to report the nomination before it can be placed on the Senate’s Executive Calendar for floor consideration. The current dispute therefore centers first on getting enough committee support for that report.

claims.text: The Senate Judiciary Committee has jurisdiction over executive nominations within the Justice Department, including the attorney general nomination.
The Senate describes the Executive Calendar as the list of nominations that committees have reported and that are awaiting Senate floor action.
AP reported that Tillis backed Cornyn’s position and that a single Republican holdout on the committee could prevent Blanche from advancing, given Democratic opposition described in the report.

Forecast: Blanche’s near-term path depends on whether DOJ’s assurances satisfy Cornyn and Tillis enough for the committee to reschedule and hold its vote, according to the committee’s statement that it is working to secure sufficient support.

related_stories.title: Fauci Invokes Fifth Amendment During Senate Hearing on COVID Origins
related_stories.summary: Dr. Anthony Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right over 100 times during a contentious Senate hearing focused on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic. The hearing, led by Republican Senator Rand Paul, included accusations that Fauci misled Congress and the public. In response, Fauci described the pursuit against him as an 'unhinged obsession.'

related_stories.title: Ceuta Requests National Emergency Amid Surge of Migrants from Morocco
related_stories.summary: Authorities in Ceuta have requested Spain to declare a national emergency due to a significant influx of migrants swimming from Morocco. The local government is seeking military assistance as border security is overwhelmed by the number of individuals attempting to enter the territory.

related_stories.title: 150-Year-Overdue Book Returned to Australian Library After Being Found in Fireplace
related_stories.summary: A book titled 'Antiquities of Athens,' published in 1858, was returned to the Kiama library in Australia after being discovered bricked inside a fireplace during home renovations. The man who found the book reported it was inside a tea crate sealed within the wall. The return marks an estimated 150 years of overdue status.

related_stories.title: Iran Promises Retaliation After US Conducts Major Strikes in Response to Attacks
related_stories.summary: Iran has vowed to retaliate against the United States following a significant military response from the US, which included a 'heavy wave of strikes' targeting Iranian positions. This action was taken in retaliation for Iran's missile attack on US forces stationed in Jordan. The strikes mark a resurgence in hostilities in the region, complicating ongoing peace negotiations and drawing in Iranian proxies.
